los-cabos.overview: Los Cabos offers modest but rugged desert and mountain trails away from the resorts. The best walking is in the Sierra de la Laguna mountains, where long day hikes reach pine forests and sweeping views of the Baja peninsula. Closer to the coast, short desert paths explore canyons and scrubland. The season runs from late fall through early spring to avoid extreme heat.

months.1: The coolest months offer the best conditions for long hikes in the Sierra de la Laguna. Clear skies and mild temperatures keep desert and mountain trails comfortable.
months.2: Dry, mild days continue, with cool air in the Sierra de la Laguna pine forests and comfortable walking on the lower desert trails.
months.8: Hurricane season brings high humidity, intense heat and the risk of heavy rain or washouts, so most trails are too hot or unpredictable.
months.9: Hurricane risk stays high, and sticky heat and possible flash floods in desert arroyos leave most trails uncertain for serious walking.
months.12: Winter brings ideal hiking weather back to the peninsula. The Sierra de la Laguna routes are fully accessible for long day hikes.

luangprabang.overview: Laos offers rugged jungle trails and steep limestone viewpoint hikes, mostly in the northern mountains. The main draws are the day hikes around Nong Khiaw, where steep climbs lead to the Pha Daeng and Pha Noy viewpoints above the Nam Ou River and karst peaks, each taking a few hours in humid heat. Multi-day village-to-village treks also run through the northern forests, though heat and monsoon rains dictate when trails are passable.

months.1: The cool and dry weather makes this the best time for the steep climb up to the Pha Daeng viewpoint. Trails are firm and temperatures are comfortable for jungle walking.
months.12: Excellent walking conditions with cool mornings and dry trails. The steep climbs to the limestone peaks are manageable, and the panoramic views are at their best.

madagascar.overview: Madagascar offers day hikes through deep sandstone canyons and limestone pinnacles. The best walking is found in Isalo National Park, where mandatory guides lead hikers past gallery forests and natural pools, and in Andringitra for multi-day treks to Pic Boby. The dry months from April to November provide the most reliable trail access.

months.9: Temperatures begin to rise, but the trails remain dry and accessible for all routes.

maldives.overview: Walking here means short island loops and sandbank strolls rather than traditional trails. Visitors take a boat to reach stretches like the long sandbank at Dhigurah. The dry months from December to April offer the calmest conditions for exploring the islands on foot.

months.1: Dry, sunny weather suits a short walk along the sandbanks and island perimeters.
months.2: Calm, dry days make boat trips to a walkable sandbank easy, and island loops are comfortable underfoot.
months.3: Dry weather holds, though heat builds, so short walks are best at the start or end of the day.
months.6: Heavy showers and strong winds frequently disrupt boat access and make narrow sandbanks unsafe to walk.
months.7: Wind and rain keep boat trips unpredictable, so sandbank walks are often called off.
months.8: Squalls continue to disrupt boat access, and only sheltered island loops are reliable.
months.9: Showers and gusts continue, with only brief calm spells for a short walk on an island loop.

months.7: Intense summer heat makes exposed mountain trails and long treks punishing and largely unappealing by midday.

months.2: February offers excellent, warm conditions for coastal walking. Water taxis make it easy to reach day sections of the Abel Tasman Coast Track or the Queen Charlotte Track.
months.5: May brings cooler weather and shorter days, but the low-elevation coastal trails remain fully walkable. It is a good time for walks along the Abel Tasman Coast Track.
months.7: July is the coolest month, but the region's mild climate means the coastal trails remain accessible. Day hikers should check water taxi schedules before they go.
months.10: October brings milder weather and longer days, ideal for walking the Abel Tasman Coast Track or the Queen Charlotte Track.

maui.overview: Maui offers two distinct hiking environments: the high-altitude volcanic landscape of Haleakalā and the lush rainforests of the coast. The standout route is the Sliding Sands Trail, which descends into the Haleakalā crater and requires a demanding climb back out at elevation. On the wetter eastern side, the Pipiwai Trail leads through a dense bamboo forest to the towering Waimoku Falls.

months.8: The warmest temperatures demand early starts for any long crater hikes, as the high-altitude sun is intense.
